references_named: Tehching Hsieh, One Year Performance 1980-1981 (Time Clock Piece)
rationale: The mechanism enacts the concept: a punch button gated to the first 60 seconds of each hour, with a year-grid that retroactively marks every elapsed un-punched hour as a permanent miss. The system clock manufactures absence on its own, which is precisely Hsieh's paradox — the misses are the proof — translated into web-native logic. The piece is materially distinct from the catalogue: it is not a Kawara date painting (Today already covers that), and no existing work restages Hsieh's time-clock discipline. Tone is dry and cheerful-cynic; license and attribution are stated; no network, no trackers. The double-coding lands: a humiliating punch-clock gag on the surface, a precise durational-performance argument underneath.
reservations: The localStorage anchor means the 'performance' is bound to first-visit hour, which slightly softens the rigor — a user who clears storage gets a fresh start, and the piece acknowledges this as the punchline rather than a flaw. The 8,760-cell grid is visually legible but the canvas resolution (146x60) is modest; the work could be slightly tighter on the 'current hour' highlight (yellow) which is a small visual flourish not strictly needed.
revision_suggestion: Consider making the 'current hour' cell visually identical to 'not yet' so the only color states are punched/missed/future — purer P3 restraint. Optionally surface the Hsieh 8,627/133 ratio as a static reference line in the grid so the comparison is structural rather than only in the footer.
